name: CA-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with an 18-point partisan lean
DeSaulnier is a well-funded incumbent with no outside opposition spending
Prediction markets price DeSaulnier at about 96% to win
No public polling, but challenger Frese has shown no measurable fundraising
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to DeSaulnier: an 18-point Democratic lean, a two-point incumbency edge, and a solid fundraising advantage with no outside money against him. Markets price this as a near-certain Democratic hold, and nothing in the evidence suggests movement away from that.
model.watch: Any sign of challenger fundraising or outside Republican spending in the district would be the first signal of a real race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mark DeSaulnier seeks another term in a Bay Area district that leans Democratic by 18 points. He enters the general with a large fundraising edge, roughly $586,000 on hand, and no outside groups spending against him. Challenger Jeff Frese reports no fundraising totals, leaving him little visible capacity to compete.

Prediction markets give DeSaulnier about a 96% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the outlook rests on the district's strong partisan lean, the incumbent's advantages, and the challenger's lack of resources, all pointing to a comfortable Democratic hold.
